Plan how many records to audit from a random pilot

Source: R/audit-plan.R
catmech_audit_plan.Rd

Answers "how many records should we audit?" for linear multiple imputation with the recorded value, [catmech_reference()] with `use_recorded = TRUE`. It predicts how much wider the interval for one regression coefficient will be at each audit fraction than with a full audit, using the classical two-phase form `width(f) = width_full * sqrt(1 + k * (1 - f) / f)`. It predicts precision only. It says nothing about bias or coverage, and it does not replace [catmech_recording_audit()].

Usage

catmech_audit_plan(
  data,
  value,
  reference,
  predictors,
  formula,
  term,
  fractions = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
  target_ratio = 1.25,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  bootstrap = 500L,
  m = 20L,
  seed = 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame holding every record in the cohort, audited or not.

value

Name of the numeric recorded value, with `NA` where nothing was recorded.

reference

Name of the numeric reference value, observed on the pilot audit only. The pilot must be a random sample of the records.

predictors

Complete auxiliary columns available on every record, as in [catmech_reference()]. Include the analysis outcome.

formula

The planned linear analysis, as passed to [catmech_pool_lm()]. It must be linear in `value`, so transform the column first rather than writing `log(value)`.

term

Name of the coefficient the audit is meant to protect.

fractions

Audit fractions to report, each above zero and at most one.

target_ratio

Width relative to a full audit that counts as good enough, above one. Default 1.25, meaning within 25% of the full-audit width.

conf_level

Level of the analysis interval and of the plan's intervals.

bootstrap

Bootstrap replicates of the pilot, at least 100.

m

Imputations for the pilot's own fits, at least two.

seed

Nonnegative integer seed. The caller's RNG state is restored.

Value

A list with:

`status`

`"no_flags"` or `"review_flags"`.

`flags`

Short names of every warning raised.

`k`

One row each for `recorded` (keep the recorded value, linear MI) and `discard` (the [catmech_reference()] default): `estimate`, `lower`, `upper`, `classical`, the empirical version described below, and `rubin_check`, the value implied by the pilot fit's own between-imputation variance.

`table`

One row per fraction: `fraction`, `records`, `additional_records` beyond the pilot, `small_audit`, which marks a size the function would refuse as a pilot, `relative_width` with `relative_lower` and `relative_upper` from the bootstrap interval for `k`, `predictive_lower` and `predictive_upper` for the width a single audit of that size may realize, `width` with `width_lower` and `width_upper` anchored on the pilot fit, and the same for discarding recorded values: `discard_relative_width`, `discard_relative_lower`, `discard_relative_upper` and `discard_width`.

`answer`

Records needed to reach `target_ratio`: `fraction` and `records` from the estimate, `records_lower` and `records_upper` from the interval for `k`, and `smallest_grid_fraction`, the smallest of `fractions` predicted to reach it, or `NA`.

`pilot`

The pilot's size, disagreements, fits and diagnostics.

`assumptions`

The assumptions the plan rests on, as text.

Details

Classical theory for an efficient two-phase estimator gives `Var(f) / Var(1) = 1 + k * (1 - f) / f` with `k = Var(psi - E[psi | aux]) / Var(psi)`, where `psi` is the influence function of the coefficient using true values and `aux` is what is known on every record. This is not a new result.

The planner evaluates that ratio under the working models, because the interval from Rubin's rules comes from them. The numerator is `Var(psi | aux)` under the normal linear imputation model fitted on the pilot's reference rows, averaged over all records. The denominator is `Var(psi)` under the homoskedastic analysis model. The result has a closed form and needs no simulation. The `classical` column instead uses empirical variances on the pilot rows. On unequal-variance data the two differ: the first describes the reported interval and the second the true sampling variance. Use `estimate` to plan interval width.

`width` is anchored on the pilot's own fit: its within-imputation variance estimates the full-audit variance, and `relative_width` scales the result. The pilot's total width is not the anchor, because its between-imputation variance is too noisy with few imputations.

Assumptions: the pilot is a simple random sample of these records; the analysis is linear MI with Rubin's rules through [catmech_pool_lm()]; the reference is exact and measures the same quantity; the later audit is random and is imputed from the same model. The formula is a large-sample one. It understates small audits, most of all when discarding recorded values, because little data then drives a large share of the variance.

The intervals answer different questions. `relative_lower` and `relative_upper` come from a bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap for `k`, so they describe the expected width. A single small audit can land far from that, because its own residual variance is noisy; `predictive_lower` and `predictive_upper` try to include this. A pilot can miss rare errors altogether, and then both ranges are too low and too narrow, so neither is a guarantee.

The function refuses a pilot with fewer than 30 rows holding both values or fewer than 20 residual degrees of freedom in the imputation model, and a pilot design that is rank deficient. It warns below 100 rows or 10 disagreements, when no pilot row disagrees, when the pilot looks selective on the recorded value (either z above 3.29, for its mean or spread), and when the outcome is missing from `predictors`. It also warns when gross errors could distort a linear fit: a pilot discrepancy above 5 robust SDs of the reference, or a recorded value above 10 robust SDs from the median. Linear MI failed in the synthetic gross-error cell of the contamination study, so do not rely on a plan carrying that warning.

Examples

set.seed(123)
n <- 120
df <- data.frame(
  outcome = stats::rnorm(n, 10, 2),
  lab = stats::rnorm(n, 5, 1),
  age = stats::rnorm(n, 50, 10)
)
df$ref <- df$lab + stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.2)
df$ref[41:n] <- NA
plan <- catmech_audit_plan(df, value = "lab", reference = "ref",
                           predictors = c("age", "outcome"), formula = outcome ~ lab + age,
                           term = "lab", bootstrap = 100L, m = 2L, seed = 1L)
#> Warning: Small pilot: k rests on 40 rows, so its interval is wide. Below 100 rows, plan on the upper limit.
summary(plan)
#> -- Catmech Audit Size Plan --
#> Target ratio:       <= 1.25x full-audit width
#> Recommended audit:  8 records (fraction: 0.067) [95% CI: 6, 13]
#> Pilot audit:        40 / 120 records (disagreements: 40)
#> Status:             review_flags
#> Flags:              small_pilot
#> 
#> Relative width across planned fractions:
#>  fraction records additional_records relative_width relative_lower
#>      0.05       6                  0          1.328          1.246
#>      0.10      12                  0          1.167          1.123
#>      0.25      30                  0          1.058          1.043
#>      0.50      60                 20          1.020          1.014
#>      0.75      90                 50          1.007          1.005
#>  relative_upper predictive_lower predictive_upper
#>           1.487            1.001            3.762
#>           1.254            1.000            2.331
#>           1.091            1.000            1.295
#>           1.031            1.000            1.126
